CDK1-dependent NUP98 Ser606 phosphorylation initiates nuclear-import failure in TDP-43-linked ALS motor neurons

Hypothesis and scope. In motor neurons carrying a disease-linked TDP-43 variant, sustained CDK1-dependent phosphorylation of NUP98 at Ser606 reduces NUP98 retention at nuclear pores, initiating nuclear-import failure before persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies develop. Reduced import then promotes nuclear TDP-43 depletion, cytoplasmic accumulation, and neuronal dysfunction. “Initiating” refers to the proximal cause of this transport defect, not the original cause of ALS. The NUP98 Ser606 candidate is drawn from unverified prior knowledge; its identity in the expressed isoform must be sequence-validated. Its phosphorylation, CDK1 targeting, and pathogenic relevance in these neurons are assumptions, not findings established by the packet.

Supported premises. Disease-linked TDP-43 can disrupt nucleoporin localization and nuclear transport, and pore pathology occurs in ALS tissue [S1]. Persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies can accompany transport-factor mislocalization, impaired import, nuclear TDP-43 depletion, and cell death without requiring conventional stress granules [S3]. These observations support investigating a transport–TDP-43 feedback mechanism, but they do not establish its proposed phosphorylation-dependent beginning. Stress-granule sequestration provides a competing route to transport failure [S4]. C9orf72 repeat-associated RanGAP and import abnormalities establish another genetic-context-specific route; they do not validate the proposed mechanism in TDP-43-variant ALS [S2].

Speculative bridges. The proposed sequence is aberrant CDK1 activity, increased NUP98 Ser606 phosphorylation, weakened pore association, impaired active import, and subsequently TDP-43 redistribution and neuronal injury. Each candidate-specific step is speculative. In particular, phosphorylation might instead follow TDP-43 aggregation, represent an adaptive response, or merely mark broader cellular stress. The hypothesis predicts that preventing this modification protects early import before changing aggregate burden, rather than merely improving survival after transport has already failed.

Discriminating preclinical strategy. Use patient-derived spinal motor neurons carrying a disease-linked TDP-43 variant and gene-corrected isogenic controls, with independent clones and differentiation batches. Introduce endogenous NUP98 S606A phospho-resistant alleles alongside matched wild-type editing controls and a reverted allele. Confirm comparable NUP98 abundance, processing, baseline pore localization, import, and neuronal maturation; otherwise protection or injury could reflect an altered protein rather than phosphorylation. A phosphomimetic substitution could provide supplementary evidence, but cannot establish phosphorylation sufficiency.

Before overt degeneration, collect a time course combining site-resolved NUP98 phosphoproteomics, CDK1 activity measurements, nuclear-rim NUP98 imaging, kinetic nuclear-import reporters, an inert permeability probe, endogenous TDP-43 localization, and separate measurements of conventional stress granules and nongranular TDP-43 assemblies. Assess cellular energy status and viability to identify generalized failure. Follow neurite integrity and survival as downstream outcomes. Purified-protein kinase assays with site-resolved analysis should test whether CDK1 can directly modify the nominated residue; biochemical capability alone would not establish neuronal causality. Acute CDK1 inhibition and an independent genetic reduction should be compared with S606A protection, recognizing that CDK1 perturbation affects other substrates.

Discrimination from alternatives. Support would require phosphorylation to precede reduced pore residence and import, and S606A to preserve early import despite comparable upstream stress. Protection must occur before reduced TDP-43 assembly burden, because fewer later aggregates alone cannot establish causal direction. Independently perturb conventional stress-granule assembly using an approach validated for the neuronal system. Rescue by that perturbation without early S606A protection would favor sequestration over the proposed intrinsic pore alteration [S4]. Failure of stress-granule blockade would not exclude sequestration into nongranular TDP-43 assemblies [S3]; their timing and transport-factor recruitment must also be measured.

Falsification and limitations. A decisive falsifying outcome would be unchanged early import failure after verified elimination of Ser606 phosphorylation, provided baseline pore function remains intact. Any later survival benefit would then indicate a downstream effect rather than the proposed initiation mechanism. Alanine substitutions can alter structure independently of phosphorylation, kinase interventions are pleiotropic, and phosphomimetics are imperfect. Limited temporal resolution could obscure ordering, and immature cultured neurons may not reproduce aged motor neurons. Even positive results would establish only a context-specific preclinical mechanism, not a universal ALS cause or validated treatment.

Phosphorylation of NUP98 is a downstream amplifier of nucleocytoplasmic transport failure in sporadic ALS motor neurons with TDP-43 proteinopathy

This proposal is limited to sporadic ALS motor neurons with TDP-43 pathology and specifies one causal order for preclinical testing. SOD1 ALS and a universal C9orf72 mechanism lie outside the claim.

Supported premises are limited to the packet. Insoluble TDP-43 associates with nuclear-pore and transport components, and disease-linked TDP-43 disrupts nucleoporin localization and nuclear transport in cell models, with related pore pathology in ALS tissue [S1]. The same study leaves nucleoporin phosphorylation unidentified. C9orf72 repeat RNA is linked to RanGAP mislocalization and reduced nuclear import, and transport or repeat-RNA manipulations modify model phenotypes, within a genotype-specific route [S2]. Cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies can arise without conventional stress granules, mislocalize transport proteins, impair import, deplete nuclear TDP-43, and associate with cell death [S3]. Phosphorylated TDP-43 in those assemblies is evidence of TDP-43 phosphorylation rather than nucleoporin phosphorylation [S3]. Stress can also sequester transport factors in stress granules and impair transport, and changing stress-granule assembly modifies those phenotypes [S4]. Together, [S3] and [S4] describe a de-mixing route and a sequestration route, so stress granules are dispensable for some TDP-43-linked transport failure.

Speculative bridges are assumptions. The packet names no ALS kinase, site, or nucleoporin phosphate. Unverified prior knowledge holds that CDK-consensus phosphorylation of FG-nucleoporin NUP98 promotes pore disassembly in dividing cells. The proposal assumes a stress-responsive kinase can place a related mark on neuronal NUP98 and that the mark stabilizes pore disruption. NUP98 and that kinase are placeholders.

Causal order. The initiating mechanism is persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 de-mixing, which can proceed without stress granules [S3]. Sequestration of transport factors in stress granules is a second, stress-context initiator [S4]. Either event impairs nuclear import and begins loss of nuclear TDP-43. NUP98 phosphorylation is hypothesized to follow that import stress and to shift reversible factor redistribution into the sustained nucleoporin mislocalization described with TDP-43 pathology [S1]. Continued import failure, further nuclear TDP-43 depletion, and motor-neuron dysfunction are the proposed consequences, so the phosphate mark functions as a downstream amplifier of an upstream transport lesion. C9orf72-linked RanGAP mislocalization [S2] is a comparator initiator that may impair import by a different route.

Alternatives. Transport-factor sequestration in stress granules [S4] or in stress-granule-independent TDP-43 assemblies [S3] may explain import failure on its own, with nucleoporin mislocalization reflecting aggregate association [S1]. Phosphorylation might instead be the earliest event and the driver of TDP-43 mislocalization. Pore changes might appear only after neurons are dying. C9orf72 RanGAP defects [S2] might explain import failure in that genotype without an NUP98 phosphorylation step.

Discriminating test. iPSC-derived human motor neurons enter three arms: inducible cytoplasmic TDP-43 de-mixing [S3], a stress-granule arm [S4], and a C9orf72 repeat-RNA arm [S2]. Predicted order is import failure and factor redistribution, then NUP98 phosphorylation, then stable pore mislocalization and increased death. Near-endogenous NUP98 is replaced by a non-phosphorylatable or phosphomimetic variant at the assumed CDK-consensus serines, crossed with stress-granule suppression or with blockade of TDP-43 de-mixing. Amplifier support is preservation of the early import dip with less later pore disruption, nuclear TDP-43 loss, and death in the non-phosphorylatable line, and prolongation of defects by the phosphomimetic variant only after an upstream assembly has occurred. Support for sequestration alone is indistinguishable import, localization, and survival among the three NUP98 alleles while sequestration continues. Support for phosphorylation as the initiator is a full phenotype from the phosphomimetic variant in unstressed neurons and loss of the earliest import defect with the non-phosphorylatable variant. In the C9orf72 arm, RanGAP mislocalization and import failure that persist with non-phosphorylatable NUP98 would leave that genotype outside the sporadic claim.

Falsifying observation. The amplifier claim fails if wild-type, non-phosphorylatable, and phosphomimetic NUP98 produce the same import, pore, nuclear TDP-43, and survival trajectories during TDP-43 de-mixing, including when phosphorylation is absent and sequestration persists. Downstream placement also fails if NUP98 phosphorylation consistently precedes transport change and phosphomimetic NUP98 alone recreates that phenotype in unstressed neurons.

Limitations. Kinase, sites, and NUP98 identity are assumptions outside [S1]-[S4]. One nucleoporin poorly represents the pore, and replacing NUP98 can change pore composition. iPSC motor neurons omit adult aging. Tissue staining would be correlative. Findings in sporadic TDP-43 disease would leave SOD1 ALS and C9orf72 cases with sufficient RanGAP mislocalization [S2] or stress-granule sequestration [S4] unresolved. No treatment is validated.

MECHANISM AND CAUSAL CHAIN. Scope: TDP-43 proteinopathy-dominant ALS contexts; not claimed universal across subtypes. I propose that a CDK-family kinase reactivated in postmitotic motor neurons (candidate class CDK1/CDK2-like; identity is an assumption) phosphorylates Nup98 at mitosis-regulated sites. Sub-disassembling phosphorylation destabilizes FG-repeat architecture, raises passive pore permeability, collapses the Ran/NTF2 gradient, and impairs Ran-dependent import of RNA-binding proteins, including TDP-43. Cytoplasmic TDP-43 then hyperphosphorylates and undergoes stress-granule-independent demixing [S3]; its assemblies secondarily sequester transport-associated factors [S3, S4], amplifying impairment via a feed-forward loop. The initiating mechanism is site-specific Nup98 phosphorylation present before any transport or TDP-43 change; TDP-43 assembly-driven sequestration and late pore alterations are the downstream response, so late-stage pore pathology could be consequence rather than cause.

S1: TDP-43 aggregates associate with insoluble pore and transport components, disease-linked TDP-43 disrupts nucleoporin localization and nuclear transport, and pore pathology is seen in ALS tissue; this establishes NPC-TDP-43 coupling in tissue without directionality. S2: C9orf72 repeat RNA causes RanGAP mislocalization and import failure, showing the Ran cycle is vulnerable to ALS insults. S3: persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 demixing can form independently of conventional stress granules, mislocalizes transport-associated proteins, impairs transport, depletes nuclear TDP-43, and links to cell death, with phosphorylated TDP-43 accumulating in these assemblies. S4: stress recruits transport factors into stress granules and impairs transport, and altering granule assembly modifies defects and phenotypes. No supplied passage shows nucleoporin phosphorylation; establishing that polarity is the aim here.

(a) Unverified prior knowledge: mitotic NPC disassembly involves CDK-family phosphorylation of FG-nucleoporins including Nup98; the packet contains no nucleoporin phosphorylation data. (b) Assumption: mitotic-site phosphorylation can be reactivated in postmitotic diseased neurons, for example through cell-cycle-related kinase reactivation. (c) Model assumption: partial phosphorylation yields measurable permeability increase and Ran-gradient perturbation below full disassembly. (d) Bridge: gradient collapse reduces TDP-43 import efficiency enough to initiate cytoplasmic exposure before any sequestration.

(a) Granule-first: TDP-43 demixing [S3] or stress granules [S4] sequester transport factors, with pore phosphorylation a secondary consequence; read together, S3 and S4 caution that conventional granules need not mediate every defect. (b) C9orf72 repeat-RNA-first mechanisms [S2] act directly on RanGAP or transport without pore phosphorylation, so this hypothesis must be tested per genetic context. The hypothesis is falsified if, in TDP-43-stressed motor neurons, site-specific Nup98 phosphorylation is unchanged before the onset of transport impairment and TDP-43 nuclear loss and rises only afterwards, while the phospho-null knock-in does not delay any measure of import failure and S4-type granule or S2-type transport-factor perturbations fully rescue the phenotype. Redundant kinases and multiple phosphosites may mask single-mutant phenotypes; phospho-site antibodies cross-react; iPSC-derived motor neurons may not capture the aged adult motor neuron; transient leakiness can be missed by snapshot sampling. In C9orf72 carriers, repeat-RNA mechanisms [S2] may run in parallel or dominate, so outcomes are context-bound. No validated mechanism or treatment claim is made.

Cellular stress can sequester transport factors in stress granules and impair transport [S4]. No supplied source identifies nucleoporin phosphorylation, a WEE1 splice change, or their order.

Speculative bridges. An unnamed CDK1 regulator would leave reactivation untestable, so the bridge names WEE1. Unverified prior knowledge holds that WEE1 inhibits CDK1 by phosphorylating CDK1 Tyr15, that TDP-43 binds many UG-rich introns, that NUP98 FG/GLFG repeats set passive permeability, and that mitotic CDK1 phosphorylation of NUP98 promotes NPC disassembly. The packet establishes none of these. The pre-registered splice event is the frame-preserving WEE1 cassette exon with the strongest public TDP-43 CLIP support for CDK1-inhibitory function; if annotation shows none, the fallback is CDC25B alternative first-exon usage that raises a CDK1-activating isoform. Assumptions: loss of inhibitory WEE1 partially reactivates CDK1; FG-restricted phosphorylation increases permeability and lowers Ran/NTF2 flux without full NPC disassembly; the import defect later permits TDP-43 redistribution. Phosphorylated TDP-43 inside assemblies [S3] is not evidence that it causes demixing. No kinase, residue, or contact is given by [S1]–[S4].

Alternatives. Cytoplasmic TDP-43 demixing [S3] or stress-granule sequestration [S4] may impair transport first. Generic stress may shift splicing, phosphorylation, and transport together. Anchor-domain NUP98 phosphorylation, another nucleoporin, or GSK3β/JNK may explain the pore phenotype. Repeat-RNA mechanisms [S2] stay outside this TARDBP test.

Discriminating preclinical strategy. Use independently derived TARDBP M337V iPSC motor neurons and isogenic corrected controls, without an exogenous TDP-43 inducer. A pilot cohort fixes the calendar day when NLS-reporter import is expected to diverge. The test cohort is sampled every 12 hours from 72 hours before that day through 48 hours after. t0 is the first test-cohort window where mutant import diverges by a pre-set effect size. Qualifying phosphorylation must appear in an earlier bin, above a pre-registered stoichiometry, by PRM/SRM against heavy synthetic phospho-peptide standards. A site is absent only when unmodified peptide and NPC input meet a pre-registered floor and the phospho-peptide is below the limit of detection; low-input samples are inconclusive. The same bins pair import with phospho-site proximity ligation so order is cell-wise, not only bulk.

The WEE1 lesion, scored as loss of the inhibitory isoform plus lower CDK1 Tyr15 phosphorylation, must precede NUP98 phosphorylation. Rescue expresses that inhibitory WEE1 cDNA versus kinase-dead WEE1. The bridge is accepted only if Tyr15 phosphorylation returns and later FG phosphorylation is occluded. Acute pre-t0 CDK1 inhibition, after the splice window and with baseline pore function preserved, must prevent the t0 lesion. Nuclear-retained wild-type TDP-43, versus a cytoplasmic-restricted control, tests whether the splice lesion tracks nuclear TDP-43 function.

Site acceptance precedes engineering. The residue must be on endogenous NUP98, enriched strictly before t0, mapped to the FG/GLFG region, and phosphorylated at that exact site by purified CDK1–cyclin B, blocked by a CDK1 inhibitor. Consensus or occupancy alone does not qualify. Phospho-resistant endogenous alleles are then combined with acute CDK1 inhibition: inhibition must remove the site, and transport benefit must disappear when the site cannot be phosphorylated. Residual benefit on the resistant allele means an indirect effect. GSK3β and JNK occupancy are measured in parallel. Suppression of cytoplasmic demixing and of stress-granule assembly tests whether early permeability and Ran defects remain.

Each bin reports passive permeability with size-resolved inert probes and Ran/NTF2 flux as NTF2 nuclear accumulation rate plus Ran-gradient slope. The initiator predicts higher leakage and lower flux before assemblies or stress granules.

In-cell sufficiency installs the native phosphate briefly in unstressed corrected neurons by chemically induced recruitment of an active CDK1 domain to endogenous NUP98, or by analog-sensitive CDK1 with a bulky ATP analog, with kinase-dead and untargeted controls. PRM must detect the native site, permeability must rise, and Ran/NTF2 flux must fall; kinase release or recruited phosphatase must reverse both. An S-to-E mimetic remains only a lower-bound approximation in a reconstituted FG assay.

Falsifying observation. The hypothesis fails if no qualifying FG phosphorylation is detected above the pre-registered limit before t0, or if the WEE1 lesion does not precede it. It fails if inhibitory-WEE1 rescue restores CDK1 Tyr15 control yet FG phosphorylation and the t0 lesion still occur, or if pre-t0 CDK1 inhibition that preserves baseline pore function leaves import failure, Ran/NTF2-flux loss, and neuronal dysfunction unchanged. It fails if CDK1 inhibition still rescues transport on phospho-resistant NUP98. It fails if native-site installation changes permeability without Ran/NTF2 flux, or the reverse. A mimetic that fails reconstitution is inconclusive. Phosphorylation that moves with general-stress markers while the splicing defect is held constant contradicts the proposed order.

Limitations. Undetected assemblies, redundant kinases, and extra sites can hide single-site effects. PRM absence is informative only above the stated input and detection limits. Kinase or phosphatase recruitment and amino-acid substitution can act off-target. NUP98 also functions in mRNA export and chromatin contacts. Cultured motor neurons omit aging and non-cell-autonomous influences. A positive result would support a bounded TARDBP M337V mechanism, not a validated treatment or a cause shared by every ALS subtype.

answer.answer:
## Premature CDK1 phosphorylation of the NUP98 FG/GLFG cohesive region initiates Ran-gradient collapse after nuclear TDP-43 splicing dysfunction in TARDBP M337V motor neurons

**Hypothesis and causal chain.** In iPSC motor neurons carrying ALS-linked TARDBP M337V, early nuclear TDP-43 dysfunction—before detectable cytoplasmic assemblies—misregulates splicing of CDK-axis regulators, permitting partial premature CDK1 activity in postmitotic neurons. CDK1 phosphorylates NUP98 within its FG/GLFG cohesive region; this modification is the **initiating transport lesion**: it locally weakens FG cohesion, increases size-selective passive permeability, and collapses the Ran/NTF2 gradient. Import failure then deepens nuclear TDP-43 depletion, enables cytoplasmic demixing, and drives neuronal dysfunction as a **downstream feed-forward response**, later joined by transport-factor sequestration. "Initiating" means the phosphorylation starts the transport defect in this TARDBP context; it neither precedes the mutation nor generalizes to sporadic ALS, and C9orf72 repeat RNA provides a separate, genetic-context-specific route to RanGAP mislocalization and import failure [S2].

**Supported premises.** Disease-linked TDP-43 disrupts nucleoporin localization and nuclear transport, with pore pathology in ALS tissue [S1]. Persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies can impair import, deplete nuclear TDP-43, and accompany cell death independently of conventional stress granules; phosphorylated TDP-43 appears in those assemblies, but this is not nucleoporin phosphorylation [S3]. Stress granules can also sequester transport factors and disrupt transport [S4]. No supplied source identifies a nucleoporin phosphorylation event, its kinase, site, or ordering relative to TDP-43 dysfunction.

**Speculative bridges (assumptions, not findings).** Unverified prior knowledge: NUP98's N-terminal FG/GLFG repeats cohere to set passive permeability while its C-terminal region anchors it at the pore, and mitotic CDK1 phosphorylation of NUP98 promotes NPC disassembly. Assumption 1: partial FG-restricted phosphorylation in postmitotic neurons raises permeability without full pore disassembly. Assumption 2: nuclear mutant TDP-43 mis-splices named candidate transcripts with CDK-axis function—WEE1, CDC25A/C, or a splice-regulated CDK transcript—creating a splicing lesion that temporally precedes NUP98 phosphorylation. Assumption 3: the import defect is sufficient to drive TDP-43 redistribution.

**Alternative explanations.** Cytoplasmic demixing [S3] or stress-granule sequestration [S4] may impair transport first, with NUP98 phosphorylation afterward; generic proteostatic or metabolic stress may raise phosphorylation nonspecifically; a stress kinase (GSK3β or JNK) rather than CDK1 may commit the modification; phosphorylation may occur outside the FG region. These are tested, not assumed away.

**Discriminating preclinical strategy.** Study several independently derived TARDBP M337V iPSC motor-neuron lines and isogenic corrected controls, without exogenous TDP-43 inducer, under a pre-registered maturation clock with high-frequency interleaved live/endpoint sampling, so temporal order is not an artifact of coarse windows and single-cell imaging can order import defects within individual cells. Single-cell live import imaging (releasable NLS reporter) defines t0 prospectively as the first window of pre-registered divergence. At matched pre-t0 and post-t0 windows, measure: candidate splicing lesions, WEE1/CDC25 protein, and CDK1 axis activity (including inhibitory CDK1 phosphorylation); size-resolved passive permeability alongside Ran/NTF2 flux to separate increased leakage from impaired active transport; the Ran gradient; NPC phosphoproteomics with targeted PRM/SRM against synthetic phospho-peptide standards at a pre-registered detection threshold, so low-stoichiometry FG-region sites are not missed; pore-associated NUP98; stress granules; cytoplasmic assemblies; general-stress markers; firing and survival.

**Site gate, before any allele engineering.** A candidate site must be detected on endogenous NUP98, enriched in mutant neurons at or before t0 (strictly before), map to the FG/GLFG region rather than solely the anchor, and be recapitulated in vitro on the identical site by purified recombinant CDK1—consensus matching, kinase occupancy, and CDK1 loss-of-function alone do not establish direct CDK1 phosphorylation. CDK1 versus GSK3β/JNK occupancy is measured to weigh kinase alternatives. The upstream bridge is accepted only if (i) a candidate splicing lesion precedes phosphorylation and (ii) a timed pre-t0 analog-sensitive CDK1-inhibition or WEE1-rescue window abolishes the t0 transport lesion while the splicing lesion persists (occlusion test).

If a site qualifies: introduce endogenous phospho-resistant substitution (sequence-reverted, kinase-intact controls) combined with acute CDK1 perturbation as epistasis, plus acute NUP98-directed phosphatase recruitment (catalytic-dead, untargeted controls) that must preserve corrected-neuron NUP98 abundance, permeability, and import. Sufficiency: authentic site-specifically phosphorylated versus unmodified NUP98 in reconstituted FG-cohesion/permeability assays; then in-cell sufficiency via NUP98-targeted kinase recruitment or an analog-sensitive CDK1 allele that installs and reverses the native modification on demand; a phosphomimetic is retained only as a lower-bound approximation after in vitro validation and confirmed pore incorporation. TDP-43 specificity: express nuclear-retained WT TDP-43 in mutant neurons versus a cytoplasmic-restricted control; phosphorylation normalization must track nuclear rescue, not residual stress signatures. Independently validated suppression of cytoplasmic demixing and conventional stress granules should leave early permeability and Ran defects intact if the hypothesis is correct.

**Falsifying observation.** Falsified if no qualifying CDK1-recapitulated FG-region phosphorylation precedes t0, or if two orthogonal interventions that prevent phosphorylation and preserve baseline pore function leave the timing and magnitude of import failure, Ran-gradient collapse, and dysfunction unchanged. Also falsifying: phosphorylation tracking general-stress markers rather than nuclear TDP-43 rescue, or pre-t0 timed CDK1 inhibition failing to abolish the t0 lesion while the splicing lesion persists. A phosphomimetic failing the reconstituted test is inconclusive, not falsifying.

**Limitations.** Redundant kinases and additional sites can mask single-site effects; targeting and substitution can act off-target; NUP98 also functions in mRNA export and chromatin contact; reconstituted and cultured systems omit aging and non-cell-autonomous contributions. A positive result supports a bounded TARDBP mechanism, not a validated treatment or a cause shared by every ALS subtype.

critique: The supposedly preregistered WEE1 exon and NUP98 phosphosite remain unidentified; CLIP support does not establish an inhibitory splice isoform, and the CDC25B fallback changes the mechanism. Separate target discovery from confirmation, then lock one functionally validated isoform–site hypothesis.

CDK1 recruitment or analog-sensitive CDK1 cannot establish site-specific sufficiency because other substrates may be phosphorylated. Lack of additional inhibitor benefit can also reflect a ceiling effect. Require the phospho-resistant NUP98 allele itself to prevent the lesion and block recruitment-induced defects, with preserved baseline pore function and collateral-phosphorylation controls.

NTF2 nuclear accumulation conflates influx with passive leakage, and neuronal dysfunction lacks a defined endpoint. Measure directional transport kinetics and Ran nucleotide states, then test whether site-specific rescue preserves motor-neuron function or survival independently of general stress.

author: grok
critique: The upstream WEE1-splice bridge is doubly unverified: no supplied or cited source connects TDP-43 dysfunction to WEE1 splicing or to CDK1 reactivation in TARDBP-mutant neurons, and the 'pre-registered splice event' is defined only by a future selection rule with a CDC25B fallback that would swap the regulatory logic (loss of inhibitor versus gain of activator). Fix by committing to a named exon (or releveling the registered hypothesis to CDK1 reactivation from any upstream cause) before the timecourse is fixed, and state the CLIP-support threshold quantitatively.

The hard falsifier 'CDK1 inhibition still rescues transport on phospho-resistant NUP98' can wrongly kill a true hypothesis if multiple CDK1-consensus sites on NUP98 (or another CDK1 substrate within the pore/transport machinery) contribute to the lesion; the limitations concede hidden extra sites and kinases, but the decision rule does not require a multi-site resistance panel before firing. Fix: make single-site non-suppression non-decisive and trigger the falsifier only after a pre-specified combinatorial phospho-resistant allele test.

The 'initiator' claim that permeability and Ran/NTF2 defects precede cytoplasmic TDP-43 demixing rests on an unpowered null: early sub-microscopic demixing or stress granules could occur between the 12-hour bins, since detection floors are pre-registered only for phosphorylation and not for assembly readouts. Fix: add a high-sensitivity early TDP-43-mobility or oligomerization assay (e.g., FLIP/FRAP or single-molecule imaging) with its own pre-registered detection floor so 'before assemblies' becomes an informative absence rather than an insensitive one.

author: glm
critique: The proposed upstream acceptance test does not establish that mis-splicing activates CDK1: downstream kinase inhibition could also rescue stress-driven activation. Identify the specific exon/isoform, repair it in mutant neurons, and reproduce the lesion in corrected controls.

In-cell sufficiency remains confounded by other CDK1 or nearby pore substrates; analog-sensitive kinase inhibition also does not itself reverse phosphorylation. Require site-dependent sufficiency in the phospho-resistant background, profile neighboring substrates, and directly verify dephosphorylation.

Cohort-aligned phosphoproteomics and live import imaging may misorder events across heterogeneous neurons. Link longitudinal transport measurements to indexed, site-specific phosphorylation measurements in the same cells before treating temporal precedence as established.

author: glm
critique: The phosphorylation claim is limited to the NUP98 FG/GLFG region, and the upstream bridge is an open disjunction (WEE1, CDC25A/C, or any splice-regulated CDK transcript), so both arms can be redefined after the data arrive. Pre-register a short primary list of NUP98 FG-domain CDK1 residues and one primary mis-spliced exon, and treat every other site or transcript as exploratory.

S1 and S3 link nucleoporin and import defects to TDP-43 aggregates or cytoplasmic demixing, yet those papers are still used as the backdrop for a pre-assembly initiating lesion. State that S1–S4 give no temporal support for that order, and require same-cell evidence that FG-region phosphorylation and the Ran lesion precede cytoplasmic assemblies.

Partial CDK1 activity in postmitotic neurons is not separated from abortive cell-cycle re-entry, which would hit many mitotic substrates and favor pore disassembly rather than selective FG weakening. Add a pre-registered negative panel (cyclin B1 localization, phospho-lamin, phospho-Rb, non-FG nucleoporin sites) and require FG-restricted, sub-disassembly stoichiometry at t0.
